answer: In the context of multilateral negotiations, 'orders of worth' refers to co-existing normative moral principles that actors use to assess the value of practices. These orders are plural systems that are not reducible to each other and can legitimately coexist in one social space. They provide different normative references that actors invoke to judge specific actions in various social spheres, helping them make sense of their situations and reach agreements based on a 'higher common principle.' Each order of worth follows a common underlying structure and is constituted around the assumption of the common good in a political community, offering rationales for determining the unequal moral status of community members.
